s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of disorganized speech, anxiety, and self-harm behaviors with rapid progression of cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms
salient_findings: Abrupt onset of disorganized speech and self-harm behaviors
Rapid, fluent, and nonsensical speech
Development of agitation, persecutory delusions, and hallucinations
Urinary and fecal incontinence
Severe cognitive impairment with MMSE score of 2/30 and ACE-R score of 2/100
key_facts: 74-year-old right-handed woman
5-month history of symptoms
Symptoms began after a family trip
History of depression treated with sertraline
No prior cognitive impairment or neurological disease
Disoriented to time
Anomia and perseveration on Clock Drawing Test
Impaired performance on Luria’s three-step test
Defective crossed-pentagon drawing
Normal brain MRI 2 months after symptom onset
Initial diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease with no clinical improvement on memantine and quetiapine

shortlist.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of disorganized speech and prominent frontal and temporal features

shortlist.label: Dementia with Lewy bodies
shortlist.why_kept: Fluctuating cognitive decline and visual hallucinations

shortlist.label: Hashimoto's encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid onset of cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms, potentially reversible

raw.rationale: The patient's rapid onset of severe cognitive and psychiatric symptoms, including disorganized speech, agitation, and hallucinations, along with the lack of prior cognitive impairment or neurological disease, and a normal brain MRI, are consistent with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, a rare neurodegenerative disorder characterized by rapid progression of dementia and neurological decline.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: While frontotemporal dementia can present with similar symptoms, its onset is typically more gradual than the 5-month history described in this case.

rejected.label: Primary progressive aphasia
rejected.why: Primary progressive aphasia is characterized by a gradual decline in language abilities, which does not match the acute onset and broad range of symptoms seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Dementia with Lewy bodies
rejected.why: Dementia with Lewy bodies often presents with visual hallucinations and fluctuating cognitive function, but the rapid progression and combination of symptoms in this case are more suggestive of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.

rejected.label: Hashimoto's encephalopathy
rejected.why: Hashimoto's encephalopathy is a rare condition associated with autoimmune thyroiditis, and while it can present with cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms, the described symptoms and normal brain MRI do not specifically point towards this diagnosis.
